captopril.t: Only ACEI labeled BID-TID for HTN (start 25 mg 2-3x/d); all 9 classmates start once daily
Neutropenia 3.7% w/ collagen vascular dz + renal impairment vs 1 in >8,600 if renal fxn normal
Rash 4-7% in first 4 wks vs 1.4% enalapril, 1.4% quinapril, 1.6% moexipril
Dysgeusia 2-4% (only sulfhydryl ACEI); no classmate label quantifies taste loss

enalapril.t: Only ACEi available IV (as enalaprilat), for hypertension when oral therapy isn't practical
Labeled for pediatric HTN from 1 month; lisinopril and benazepril start at 6 years

fosinopril.t: Dual renal+biliary clearance: usual dose at any CrCl incl ESRD; all other ACEIs need reduction

lisinopril.t: Non-prodrug (only it + captopril); no hepatic activation, excreted 100% unchanged in urine
Only ACEI labeled for acute MI itself: 5 mg within 24 h, not just post-MI LV dysfunction

moexipril.t: Take 1 h before meals — food cuts Cmax ~70%, AUC ~40%; largest food effect in the class

perindopril.t: Labeled for stable CAD (EUROPA): CV death/MI/arrest 9.9% to 8.0%; lisinopril lacks this
Elderly: sparse data >8 mg/day though max is 16; lisinopril needs no age adjustment

quinapril.t: Quinapril tablet's magnesium content cuts tetracycline absorption 28-37%; only ACEI so labeled
Only ACEI on FDA shortage list - Current since 1/2023, still listed 8/2026

ramipril.t: HOPE: 10 mg cut MI/stroke/CV death 17.8% to 14.0%; only ACEI indicated in DM/PAD, not just CAD

trandolapril.t: Label starting dose is race-stratified: 1 mg non-Black, 2 mg Black — unique among ACEIs
PEACE was neutral in stable CAD (21.9% vs 22.5%, P=0.43); perindopril's EUROPA was positive

azilsartan.t: 80 mg cut placebo-adj 24-h SBP -14.3 mmHg vs olmesartan 40 -11.7 and valsartan 320 -10.0
First true US generic Jun 2026 (Lupin, 180-day exclusivity); other 6 ARBs generic for years

candesartan.t: Only ARB with 2 positive migraine-prevention RCTs; 16 mg non-inferior to propranolol 160 mg
CHARM-Alternative: HR 0.77 for CV death/HF admit in 2028 ACEi-intolerant HFrEF pts

irbesartan.t: IDNT: 37% less Cr doubling vs amlodipine, matched BP; only ARB w/ active-comparator renal RCT

losartan.t: Uricosuric via URAT1: SUA -63 vs -12 umol/L on irbesartan at 8 wk, n=351
Only ARB labeled to cut stroke in HTN+LVH; label says benefit not in Black patients
Shortest t1/2 in class (2 h; E-3174 6-9 h); label: BID beats same total once-daily dose
Only ARB needing CYP2C9 activation: fluconazole cuts active E-3174 AUC 40%

olmesartan.t: Only ARB labeled for sprue-like enteropathy: severe diarrhea + weight loss, months-years in
ROADMAP: fatal CV events 15 (0.7%) vs 3 (0.1%) on placebo, p=0.01, in normoalbuminuric T2DM
No CV outcome indication, unlike telmisartan, losartan, valsartan and candesartan

telmisartan.t: Longest t½ in class ~24 h vs candesartan 9 h, valsartan 6 h, losartan 2 h
Only ARB with a digoxin interaction: Cmax +49%, trough +20% — check levels on start/stop
Only ARB indicated to cut MI/stroke/CV death in high-risk pts unable to take an ACEi

valsartan.t: Food cuts AUC ~40%, Cmax ~50%; irbesartan, candesartan, azilsartan food-independent
Only ARB with a labeled post-MI indication: cuts CV mortality with LV dysfunction (VALIANT)
HF and post-MI dosing is BID (to 160 mg BID); candesartan's HF dose stays once daily

atenolol.t: Renal cap: max 50 mg/d if CrCl 15-35, 25 mg/d if <15 - only BB here with a hard dose ceiling
Hemodialysis: 25-50 mg after each session, under supervision - marked BP falls

betaxolol.t: Half-life 14-22 h, longest in class; metoprolol tartrate 3-7 h, propranolol 3-6 h

bisoprolol.t: ~50% renal / 50% hepatic elimination — atenolol is renal-only, metoprolol/carvedilol hepatic

carvedilol.t: Digoxin levels +15%; cyclosporine dose cut ~20% in 30% of pts; classmates show no such PK hits
GEMINI: metoprolol raised HbA1c, carvedilol did not; carvedilol improved HOMA-IR

metoprolol.t: Only succinate ER is once-daily + HF-approved; tartrate is HTN/angina/MI only, not swappable
POISE: periop metoprolol cut MI 5.7 to 4.2% but doubled stroke 0.5 to 1.0%

nebivolol.t: Label: no controlled trials showing risk reduction, unlike metoprolol succinate or carvedilol

propranolol.t: Labeled for migraine prophylaxis, essential tremor and HOCM - no classmate carries these

amlodipine.t: t½ 30–50 h — longest of the DHPs (felodipine 11–16 h, isradipine 8 h); forgives missed doses
Only DHP with a labeled statin cap: simvastatin ≤20 mg/day (verapamil/diltiazem cap at 10 mg)
Label carries CAMELOT: CV events 16.6% vs 23.1% placebo in CAD (HR 0.69) — unique in class
Grapefruit has no effect on amlodipine exposure; felodipine >2× AUC, nifedipine 2× (avoid)

felodipine.t: Background therapy in HOT (n=18,790) — outcome data isradipine and nisoldipine lack

nifedipine.t: IR capsule label: angina only — explicitly says not for control of essential hypertension
3 × 30 mg ER tablets are not interchangeable with one 90 mg ER tablet — Cmax 29% higher

nisoldipine.t: Cmax up to +245% with high-fat meal (AUC -25%); 4x nifedipine ER/felodipine, dose fasting
ABCD trial in T2DM: 25 MIs on nisoldipine vs 5 on enalapril (RR 9.5); secondary endpoint

isradipine.t: MIDAS: major vascular events 5.65% vs 3.17% on HCTZ (n=883, p=0.07)

nicardipine.t: Mild renal impairment ~doubles Cmax/AUC; other oral DHPs need no renal adjustment

diltiazem.t: Raises digoxin ~20% vs 50–75% with verapamil — the easier non-DHP for digoxin patients

verapamil.t: Raises serum digoxin 50-75% in week 1; diltiazem raises it only ~20%
Only oral non-DHP labeled for AF/flutter rate control and PSVT prophylaxis
INVEST (n=22,576): verapamil-based strategy equalled atenolol-based in CAD + HTN

hydrochlorothiazide.t: Only class member labeled for NMSC: +1 SCC/6,700 white pts/yr at cumulative dose ≥50,000 mg
t½ 5.6-14.8 h, diuresis 6-12 h vs chlorthalidone 40-60 h, up to 72 h - misses end of 24 h
HCTZ 50 mg cut night SBP 6.4 vs 13.5 mm Hg for chlorthalidone 25 mg (ABPM crossover, P=0.009)

chlorthalidone.t: DCP n=13,523: switch HCTZ→chlorthalidone, no MACE benefit, HR 1.04 (0.94-1.16), 2.4 yr
t½ 40-60 h vs 5.6-14.8 h HCTZ, ~14 h indapamide; dose changes take ~1-2 wk to show fully
Thalitone (15 mg, w/ food) is labeled NOT substitutable with other chlorthalidone formulations

indapamide.t: HYVET, age 80+: indapamide±perindopril cut all-cause death 21%, HF 64% - classmates lack this
HYVET's SR 1.5 mg isn't sold in the US; label lists only IR 1.25 and 2.5 mg

furosemide.t: PO bioavailability 64% vs torsemide 80% (CI 75-89%); underpins ~2:1 IV-to-PO conversion
Sucralfate blunts response - separate by 2 h; phenytoin cuts absorption and effect

spironolactone.t: Gynecomastia 21.2% vs eplerenone 4.5% head-to-head; dose-dependent, onset 1-2 mo to >1 yr
Beat eplerenone in primary aldo: DBP -12.5 vs -5.6 mmHg/16 wk, at lower mg doses
Food raises AUC ~95% - label says take consistently with respect to meals
Falsely elevates digoxin radioimmunoassay - use a non-interfering assay

eplerenone.t: Contraindicated w/ strong CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole AUC 5.4x); spironolactone has no bar

amiloride.t: PATHWAY-2 open-label phase: clinic SBP -20.4 mmHg on amiloride 10mg vs -18.3 on spiro 25mg

captopril: Neutropenia 3.7% with connective tissue disease plus renal impairment
olmesartan: Sprue-like enteropathy - chronic diarrhea and weight loss, months to years in
quinapril: High magnesium content cuts tetracycline absorption 28-37%
In FDA-listed shortage since 2023 - do not start new patients
hydrochlorothiazide: Squamous cell skin cancer with cumulative dose (FDA 2020) - counsel sun protection
chlorthalidone: The 2025 guideline dropped its preference - no MACE benefit over HCTZ
atenolol: Renally cleared - cap 50 mg/d if CrCl 15-35
